description: This figure group is a single dual-ordinate scatter plot; it contains no micrograph, spectrum, map or inset. The x-axis is labelled "Wt% Al" with ticks at 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9, but data exist only at 5, 6, 7 and 9 wt% Al. The left ordinate is "Volume fraction (%)" (linear, labelled 0.0 to 3.0 in 0.5 steps) and the right ordinate is "Diameter (nm)" (linear, labelled 0.0 to 4.0 in 0.5 steps). A legend at the top left defines filled circles as "Volume fraction" (to be read on the left axis) and filled squares as "Diameter" (read on the right axis). Every marker carries a vertical error bar. The volume-fraction circles rise monotonically: just below the 0.5% gridline at 5 wt% Al, between the 0.5 and 1.0% gridlines at 6 and 7 wt% Al (higher at 7), and immediately below the 2.0% gridline at 9 wt% Al. The diameter squares lie at about the 2.5 nm gridline at 5 wt% Al, between the 2.5 and 3.0 nm gridlines at 6 and 7 wt% Al, and between the 3.5 and 4.0 nm gridlines at 9 wt% Al. The figure demonstrates that both the diameter and the volume fraction of the Fe-Al ordered phase increase with Al content, the increase being steepest between 7 and 9 wt% Al.

observations.observation: The figure is a single dual-ordinate scatter plot: x-axis labelled 'Wt% Al' with ticks 5-9, left y-axis 'Volume fraction (%)' from 0.0 to 3.0 in 0.5 steps, right y-axis 'Diameter (nm)' from 0.0 to 4.0 in 0.5 steps.
The legend defines filled circles as 'Volume fraction' and filled squares as 'Diameter'.
Data points are plotted only at 5, 6, 7 and 9 wt% Al; no marker is present at the 8 wt% Al tick.

The volume-fraction (circle) series increases monotonically with Al content, from just below the 0.5% gridline at 5 wt% Al to immediately below the 2.0% gridline at 9 wt% Al, with the 6 and 7 wt% Al points lying between the 0.5 and 1.0% gridlines.
Every marker in both series carries a vertical error bar, and the error bars on the 9 wt% Al points are the largest in the figure.
The jump in volume fraction between 7 and 9 wt% Al is much larger than the rise between 5 and 7 wt% Al.
No numeric data labels are printed on any point; all values must be read against the axis gridlines.
The caption states the figure shows the variation of diameter and volume fraction of Fe Al ordered phase with changing weight percentage of Al.
The citing text states that, based on TEM and SAXS results, the ordered phase is nano-sized with sizes ranging between 2.5 and 3.75 nm (Fig. 4), which matches the span of the diameter axis data.
The citing text states that the size of the ordered phase measured from TEM is 2.1 +/- 0.2 nm and is in correlation with that determined from SAXS studies (cf. Fig. 4).
The citing text states that the fine Fe3Al ordered phase has been established by Mossbauer spectroscopy, SAXS and TEM based studies and is considered an additional strengthening mechanism.
